speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are presenting with a limp and localized pain; please tell me, how old are you and exactly where is the pain located?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The child is a 7-year-old male with left knee pain favoring that leg, and no trauma or fever. Is the pain worse with activity or at night, and does pressing on the joint itself cause tenderness?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, ESR, CRP, and Urinalysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Good news; the blood work and urinalysis are normal, which helps rule out infection or inflammatory conditions. Given the normal labs and the specific presentation of a 7-year-old boy with left knee pain favoring that leg, could you tell me if he reports pain when you press directly on the kneecap or if he has noticed any swelling there?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the labs are normal and there is no swelling or tenderness at the joint itself, do you feel pain specifically when I press on the tendons around your knee or when you straighten your leg against resistance?

REQUEST TEST: X_Knee_Lateral, X_Knee_Ap.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I have requested the lateral and AP X-rays of the left knee to evaluate the bone structure. While we wait for those results, can you tell me if the pain has been present for weeks or months, and does he have any history of recent growth spurts?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Unlikely given normal labs), Osgood-Schlatter Disease (Possible), or Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE - must rule out with X-rays).
